Review Body:
On Tyranny is a power-packed little book originally published in 2017. The book's main point is that democracy, if valued, must be defended. It is fallible. Through a series of brief essays, Timothy Snyder describes lessons from history - particularly from the fall of democracies in the 20th century - that should guide us in protecting our democracy and responding to the threats that face us today. He concludes with Lesson 20: Be as courageous as you can, with one final sentence (before the epilogue): If none of us are prepared to die for freedom, then all of us will die under tyranny.

This book was gifted to me shortly after publication, and sat on my TBR shelf gathering dust until just recently. It is a guidebook for the times were living in today, I'm afraid - and Professor Snyder surely saw in Trump's first administration the potential for the fall of our democracy. While I fear for America's future, I finished this book feeling determined to use my voice and actions to speak for what I believe in - that love and respect of all of us is right and just - with liberty and justice for all.

Not to say that our current president is the whole problem - the roots of what brought us to today are deftly described in On Tyranny - the disrespect for one another, the weakening of opposition, the disinterest in historical lessons - and on and on. So many of us have taken for granted that democracy was permanent; now I, at least, fear for it.

I strongly recommend that regardless of where you stand politically, you take the time to read On Tyranny.
